injection_probes.the_harness_itself_fault_twice_before_it: recorded because both faults are the ones this repository has already recorded once and neither is visible in the output. First, the restore path decoded raw CRLF *bytes* and then applied `.replace(chr(10), chr(13)+chr(10))` a second time, rewriting every pre-existing line ending as CR CR LF; the sha256 restore check caught it, which is the check's entire purpose, and the fix was to normalise to LF on the way in so the conversion happens once. Second, the probe anchor for the intent body occurred twice in `server_v1_api.gd`, and the harness refused it rather than mutating one of the two -- which is why that probe's anchor spans the whole function signature instead of the two lines it replaced.

injection_probes.which_guard_is_the_real_gate: two different answers, and the split is the useful part. For an invented DERIVATION the gate is the pinned whole inventory: A5 and A6 borrow no reserved stem and still score 3 each, because the inventory pin and the two count pins see them alone, while the stem-bearing A2 and A3 score 4 -- two detections for one planted line. So the reserved-stem check is the belt and the inventory is the gate there. For the ANTI-VACUITY anchor the answer inverts: A1 borrows no stem and scores 12, because the guard that catches it is not a name scan at all -- it is `_check_fail_closed`'s first statement, which parses the unmodified captured success. A name scan would not have noticed that every probe in the previous, sixteen-row table was firing against a module that refused everything.
